headline: Claude keeps shipping before checking the result, and you keep pasting the same deploy steps. Two skills and one rule would save about 3 hours a week.

history.note: Transcripts are kept for 365 days (cleanupPeriodDays = 365). Oldest session: 2026-09-12.

A.title: Says it's done before checking the result
A.detail: In 14 sessions you had to point out that the page, build or file was still broken after Claude said it was finished.
A.fix: Add a rule: after any change, run the check (tests, build, screenshot) and show the output before saying done.

quotes.text: It's still showing the old header, did you even check?
No, the build fails, look at the error first

A.title: Changes things you didn't ask to change
A.detail: Edits spill into files outside the request.
A.fix: Rule: touch only the files named in the request; ask before widening scope.

quotes.text: I never asked you to change the footer

B.title: Your stack and where things live
B.rule: This project is a Next.js 15 app. Content lives in content/, components in app/components/. Use pnpm, never npm.

quotes.text: remember we use pnpm not npm

C.name: deploy-preview
C.title: Deploy a preview and send me the link

quotes.text: deploy a preview and give me the link

D.title: Monday client status report
D.automation: A skill that drafts the report from git log and the roadmap, run every Monday 9:00 by a Desktop scheduled task; you approve before it is sent.
steps: Approve the draft each Monday before it goes to the client

quotes.text: write the weekly update for the client from what we did

summary: Biggest win: make Claude prove a change works before calling it done.
